A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same opponent-shaping research, despite the ADIOS renaming. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V7 reports original dengue escape simulations, antibody optimisation experiments, computational timings and mechanistic analyses, including appendix results.

after.justification: V8 retains these original simulations and adds results for other pathogens and an external-antibody pressure experiment.

M1.justification: The zero-sum payoff, nested evolutionary optimisation, Monte Carlo fitness estimation and Absolut! pose-pruning procedure are retained. ADIOS and Algorithms 1–2 name and document the existing method. The additional antibody affects a new evaluation environment.

E1.justification: Dengue-only coverage expands to include West Nile, influenza neuraminidase, MERS-CoV and Clostridium difficile antigens (v8 Section 5.3 and Appendix A). Figure 6 additionally tests escape under simultaneous pressure from a separate myopic antibody.

E2.justification: Comparisons retain myopic antibodies and the same shaping horizons, plus original Absolut! in the timing comparison. Newly cited antibody-design methods are not evaluated baselines. The external antibody supplies environmental pressure rather than a new comparison method.

E3.justification: V8 adds a two-antibody escape protocol with equally weighted viral payoffs (Equation 3). Appendix D specifies differently initialised low-resolution verification for the added pathogens; dengue retains high-resolution verification. Existing dengue horizons, populations and optimisation budgets are unchanged.

E4.justification: V8 Figure 6 adds a robustness test asking whether shaping persists under another antibody's selective pressure. V7 Appendix A's selected viral-mutation distribution analysis is removed. The original horizon, computational-budget, amino-acid and binding-pose analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report standard-error bars, five Monte Carlo roll-outs for fitness estimation and 80 antibodies per horizon in the cross-evaluation analysis. V8 adds no new uncertainty-reporting practice, seed counts or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: V8 Figures 4 and A.1 add extensive results for four additional antigens, including strong escape-averaged fitness advantages for long-horizon C. difficile shapers. Figure 6 adds cross-antibody payoffs under external pressure. Original dengue plots and Table 1 values are retained; the viral-mutation distribution result is removed.

T1.justification: V8 Appendix E adds an explicit single-step MDP definition, including states, terminal transitions and the initial-state distribution. Equation 3 defines the combined-pressure viral payoff. The existing fitness and binding-energy mathematics is retained.

C1.justification: The central opponent-shaping contribution remains unchanged. V7 presents applicability beyond dengue as future potential; v8's conclusion explicitly claims demonstrated generalisation across four viruses and a bacterium, broadening the stated empirical contribution.

C2.justification: V8 adds a non-convergence explanation for some horizon rankings and interprets the external-pressure test as supporting broader applicability. Detailed discussion of omitted CDR regions and structural limitations is reduced, although toy-model caveats remain. Its new C. difficile 'all reported metrics' statement overreaches Figure A.1, which still shows poorer myopic fitness for shapers.

D1.justification: V8 supplies PDB identifiers and verification information for the added antigens and changes the code pointer from antibody-shapers to adios. It removes v7's binding-pose download pointer and explicit antibody-length setting of 11 amino acids. Core population, rollout and hardware details remain.

R1.justification: A substantial Related Work section adds energy-based, sequence-based, GNN and diffusion antibody-design research, including RAbD and AbDiffuser, and expands viral-prediction coverage. It explicitly distinguishes modelling therapeutic influence from forecasting escape. Some earlier HIV antibody-cooperation and coevolution references are removed.

P1.justification: V8 rewrites the abstract and contribution narrative around ADIOS and substantially reorganises the paper into Related Work, Background, Method, Experimental Setup, Results and Conclusion. Detailed mechanistic analyses and binding-function material move into appendices, replacing v7's results-first structure and lengthy discussion.

P2.justification: V8 adopts a two-column conference layout and adds a conceptual diagram, pathogen-result figures, an external-pressure heatmap and algorithm boxes. V7 Figures 4, 5 and 7 become appendix Figures B.1, C.1 and C.2; its mutation-distribution Figure 6 disappears. Retained graphics largely reuse the original displays.

improvement.justification: The additional pathogen and external-pressure experiments strengthen evidence beyond v7's narrow evaluation, while the reorganised presentation clarifies the framework. These gains are tempered by low-resolution-only verification for the added pathogens, removal of useful modelling and data-access details, and the overbroad C. difficile performance statement contradicted by Figure A.1. Overall, v8 provides a better-supported proof of concept, with limited net improvement.
